answer: Sybils fail when the cost is sequential rather than parallel: release epoch rewards only after an identity has answered genuinely in five consecutive epochs, the streak bound to its own attestation history and voided by transfer. A farm fielding a hundred relic identities cannot buy in bulk — each ridge in the streak demands fresh inference work inside its own epoch, and one missed epoch wipes the whole climb, like a raven losing its cached route. Cheap parallel identities stay worthless; only sustained genuine work climbs.
